title: Nationalization of Dutch assets — 700 companies expropriated
reason: Well-corroborated by multiple independent sources. In response to Indonesia's failed third UN resolution on West New Guinea (West Irian) in November 1957, Sukarno's government launched a retaliatory nationalization campaign starting with a 24-hour strike against Dutch companies on December 1, 1957, followed by labor-union/army takeovers and formal nationalization decrees. Wikipedia's West New Guinea dispute article states ~700 Dutch-owned companies valued at roughly $1.5 billion were nationalized, including KLM landing rights, the KPM shipping line, oil companies BPM (Royal Dutch Shell's Indonesian subsidiary) and Borsumij, and Dutch banks/estates — directly matching the description's "700 companies including Royal Dutch Shell operations." Multiple sources corroborate expulsion of Dutch nationals in the tens of thousands (10,000 by Jan 1958 rising to 40,000-50,000 in contemporary Dutch government/press accounts), consistent with the description's "~46,000." One academic source (Economic History Review-affiliated, via tandfonline) suggested Shell/Unilever/Heineken partly evaded full nationalization by claiming "international" corporate status and only fully divested via a 1965 negotiated sale — creating some nuance on the Shell detail — but this doesn't contradict that Shell's BPM subsidiary and assets (e.g., North Sumatra fields feeding into the new state firm Permina) were seized/affected in the December 1957 wave per multiple other sources. Core facts (country, year, trigger, scale, expulsion) are solid; the Shell nuance is a minor secondary-source disagreement, not a material scope error.

title: Nickel ore export ban — downstream industrialization strategy
reason: Indonesia's nickel export ban timeline does not match the description's characterization of 2017. The original export ban was first imposed in January 2014. In 2017, Indonesia did NOT 'announce' a ban to take effect in 2020 — it did the opposite: Government Regulation 1/2017 RELAXED the existing ban, allowing companies to export nickel ore with concentration below 1.7% between January 2017 and December 2019, with a plan for the full ban to be reinstated only in January 2022.
